correctness.rationale: PASS: The negative sign coordinates cannot occupy different classes, since their cross-class sum would be negative. Given k negatives in a single class A_i, their magnitudes must precede all n-a_i outside magnitudes in an iid continuous symmetric sample, with exact probability 1/binom(n-a_i+k,k). The identity binom(a_i,k)/binom(n-a_i+k,k)=binom(n,a_i-k)/binom(n,a_i) yields the stated F_n(a_i). Uniform cube and Gaussian share this sign/rank probability, but only the Gaussian is the Euclidean solid angle; cube volume is 2^n times the probability. The k=1 term a/(n+1-a) is strictly convex and remaining factorial-ratio terms are convex; integer Robin Hood transfers then prove Schur-convex extremizers. A geometric-tail majorant at balanced a/n->1/r<1/2 and binomial symmetry at a=n-r+1 justify the distinct asymptotics. I independently recomputed exact angles 3/80 and 31/480 and all discrete second differences for 4<=n<=30. These computations corroborate—not replace—the unrestricted proof.
